suggestions: The new path derivation still assumes the resolved main entry (dist/prod/index.js) sits directly alongside a 'fonts' sibling directory — an implicit contract with @excalidraw/excalidraw's internal dist layout carried over unchanged from the old hardcoded path. Worth a one-line comment noting this assumption will break if a future major version restructures dist/ (e.g. moves the entry into a nested esm/ subfolder).
Comments are in Czech only; if the repo has non-Czech-reading contributors, a short bilingual or English note would aid maintainability (stylistic only, not required).
structured_output.summary: The fix correctly swaps a hardcoded 'node_modules/@excalidraw/excalidraw/...' path for dirname(require.resolve('@excalidraw/excalidraw')) + 'fonts'. require.resolve() only performs static path resolution via Node's module algorithm (including exports-map 'default' condition fallback) — it does not load or execute the target file, so the stated goal of resolving the package without executing its module code is met, and this works whether the package is CJS or ESM-only. createRequire(import.meta.url) anchors resolution to the script's own location and Node's resolver walks ancestor node_modules directories, so both local and hoisted installs (e.g. in a git-worktree layout) are found, matching the described RED→GREEN behavior. The derived font path (dirname(entry)+'/fonts') reproduces the exact same location the old hardcoded path pointed to, so behavior is preserved. The new pytest test faithfully simulates real package resolution (separate local vs. hoisted node_modules, a package.json with only a 'default' export condition and no package.json subpath export, a throwing index.js to prove non-execution, a path containing spaces, and content-integrity assertions for both copied and original files) and is not shell-injectable (list-form subprocess.run, shell=False). No security vulnerabilities or logic defects were found; only minor documentation-style suggestions."
